doc.title: Roswell Rudd interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998

title: Monochord, waves and the trombone
summary: Rudd describes his research into Egyptian harp orchestras and the monochord, calling the trombone an agitated string and everything waves.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Life philosophy: faith, karma and how to live

blocks.x: I’m still researching you know. For me this last year, what it’s come down to finally after a lot of research, I realized that the harp orchestras in Egypt, six, seven thousand years ago, that they had all the harmonic knowledge then that we have now, just as far as what the monochord can do. And so I’ve just been devoting myself to the monochord and I realize that the trombone is really nothing more than an E string that’s agitated with my lips and breath as opposed to plucking and bowing and all that, it’s just different, but we’re all working with the same wave. And the more that we respect the wave and the more that we know about the wave, the better chances of our getting inside the wave and becoming the wave and therefore controlling the wave. And this is our basic vehicle of communication, the wave.
Gave me something to think about on the way home.

Isn’t it all waves? It’s all waves, isn’t it? I mean solidity is an illusion. Basically there’s not a particle in the universe. You have the illusion of solidity because some particles are of lower frequencies than others. Basically what you have is a composite of an

astounding range of frequencies, from below zero to beyond infinity, and thus all this different stuff, but all this vibrating, but no particles. Nobody’s been able to find a particle yet. They keep digging, they keep digging, they think oh I’ve cornered it, there he is, there he is, and then they get in there and they find out it’s just some kind of a coincidence of different frequencies, different vibrations happening, but there’s no stuff, there’s no particles, it’s just a dance, some kind of vibration in space. Who knows? Maybe we’ll find a particle in the next two hundred years.
Maybe we will. There he is! We finally got him?
